newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO reduces 1996/97 world cereal imports forecast.
newsitem.headline: FAO reduces 1996/97 world cereal imports forecast.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday that its forecast for world cereals imports in 1996/97 has been reduced by two million tonnes since its last report to 184 million tonnes.
It said this was "sharply below the revised estimate of 202 million tonnes traded in 1995/96."

"The bulk of the reduction in world trade compared to the previous year is anticipated in wheat and coarse grains while imports of rice in 1997 are expected to contract only marginally," it said in a food outlook.

FAO said the forecast for world imports of wheat and wheat flour (in grain equivalent) in 1996/97 was now 84 million tonnes, or nine million less than in 1995/96 and the smallest volume since the late 1970s.
"This contraction is due to increased production in several countries that had been large importers in the previous year, in particular China, Morocco and the CIS," it said.
